202B.5 / CHAPTER 5 OF 11

Holder rotation

Did ownership change, or only the addresses?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Attention persistence11Market maturity & the method boundary

01Definition

Holder rotation transfers inventory from one group of owners to another.

02Why it matters

A similar-looking chart can sit above a very different ownership structure.

03What to check

  • Actual sales versus wallet transfers
  • Old and new related-wallet balances
  • Known entry costs and missing history

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Independent ownership changes are supported by traceable transactions.

Dangerous

One actor splits inventory and concentration appears to improve.

05Beginner mistake

Assuming lower top-holder percentages mean stronger holders.

06Takeaway

Verify the transfer of control.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

  3. 03

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Wallet A transfers 5m units to B. Holder count changes, but no sale occurred. If A instead sells and unrelated purchasers receive inventory through swaps, that is a different ownership change. Missing links make independence provisional.

How to investigate it

Trace transaction type and quantities, reconcile old and new balances, and investigate funding links where appropriate. Separate ordinary pool and system addresses. Use actual cost histories rather than marking every new wallet’s balance at current price as its entry cost.

Check your reasoning — answered

Ten new addresses receive inventory from one source without buying. Has ownership become organic? Not established. It may be one position split across addresses.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Use provider-reported holder count and concentration as leads. Trace actual ownership, entries, and transfers externally.

Go deeper

New holders are not automatically stronger or less likely to sell. Labels, higher estimated cost basis, and lower concentration each need supporting history, and none guarantees future behavior.
